Fig. 1
Illustrations depicting the mortise-tenon joint structure used in ancient Chinese architecture.

Figs. 2A, 2-B, and 2-C Schematic diagrams illustrating the arthroscopic inlay Bristow procedure. Fig. 2-A Coracoid plug preparation. Fig. 2-B Appearance of the trough in the glenoid. Fig. 2-C Coracoid plug fixation into the trough in the glenoid.

Figs. 3-A through 3-F Representative 3D CT images of coracoid block positioning and healing after arthroscopic inlay Bristow procedure fixed with a screw.
Figs. 3-A and 3-B Axial view (Fig. 3-A) and en face view (Fig. 3-B) demonstrating perfect coracoid positioning (below the equator) and healing 6

Figs. 4-A, 4-B, and 4-C Representative on face view of 3D-CT images showing osteolysis of coracoid grafts at the time of the latest follow-up. Fig. 4-A Grade 0: the cone of the screw head is buried in the coracoid bone graft. Fig. 4-B Grade 1: only the screw head is exposed outside the coracoid bone
